    *   *Theme:* We offer a hard cap at $285k. Unlike competitors who may quote low but bill out-of-scope for complex mapping, our fixed price includes all standard AS2/EDIFACT mappings for the 62 partners.
    *   *Evidence:* Highlight our previous success with the AP change order transparency (see Marguerite’s preference for Excel breakdowns). Show that we don’t hide costs in the fine print.

    *   *Theme:* Our implementation methodology is designed to run parallel to your current operations without requiring IT staff time from your DC teams.
    *   *Evidence:* Reference the **WWI Dallas/Memphis go-live experience**. We delivered complex hardware/software integrations (APs, Kiosks) on tight timelines (Feb/Mar) without impacting store ops. Norvik is likely a pure-play software shop; we are an end-to-end infrastructure partner.

*   **References (20%): "Proven Retail Scale"**
    *   *Theme:* We aren’t just implementing EDI; we are integrating it into live retail environments.
    *   *Evidence:* Cite **Fourth Coffee** (12 cafes, real-time kiosk integration) and **Northwind** (IoT sensor integration with TMS). These prove we can handle high-volume, real-time data flows in distributed retail settings.

*   **Support (10%): "Local & Responsive"**
    *   *Theme:* Dedicated support team familiar with your specific DC pain points.
    *   *Evidence:* Mention Stavros’ feedback on the AP vendor delay—we proactively managed the timeline shift. Norvik will likely offer generic L1/L2 support; we offer named account engineers who know your business.

**2. Where We Are Weak (And How to Mitigate)**

*   **Weakness: Pure-Play EDI Specialization**
    *   *Risk:* Norvik might be perceived as more specialized in EDI standards than us (who are broader B2B services).
    *   *Mitigation:* Emphasize that EDI is just one component of the supply chain. Our value is connecting EDI to *physical* operations (inventory, logistics). Use the **Litware Playwright** migration example to show technical depth in automation and testing.

    *   *Risk:* Underestimating the mapping effort.
    *   *Mitigation:* Provide a sample mapping matrix in the proposal. Show we’ve already analyzed the top 10 most complex partners and have a plan for them. This proves we’ve done the homework.
